offence_severity: Life imprisonment with fine / Rigorous imprisonment for four months with fine
premeditation_planning: Court found motive and common intention to kill
motive: Rivalry over agricultural land and pending court cases
key_evidence_accepted: The eye-accounts are fully supported by statement of Investigating Officer, inquest report, post mortem report and the recoveries. The presence of PW3, PW4, PW7 and PW15 at the place of occurrence is neither unnatural nor improbable. The version given by these witnesses is fully corroborated by documentary and medical evidence. The blood-stained clothes of the deceased and other articles were recovered, sealed and sent for serological examination, and human blood of blood group 'O', which was also the blood group of the deceased, was found on all the three articles.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as reliable and trustworthy, noting that their statements are fully corroborated by documentary and medical evidence. The court also stated that the testimony of an eye-witness, if found truthful, cannot be discarded merely because the eye-witness was a relative of the deceased.
trial_duration: Trial court acquitted all accused except three, High Court upheld conviction, Supreme Court dismissed appeal

legal_representation.accused: Bhagwati Prasad, H.D. Thanvi, Pushpendra Singh, Sarad Kumar Singhania
legal_representation.state: P.P. Malhotra, ASG, Wasim A Qadri, Kiran, B.K. Prasad, B.V. Balramdas, Suryanarayana Singh, Pragati Neekhra

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused caused the death of one person, with 4 eye-witnesses, animosity between parties, and that the prosecution proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. The cumulative effect of the prosecution evidence supports the conviction.
defence_argument: The appellants contended that there is contradiction between the ocular and medical evidence, contradictions and improvements in witness statements, the presence of PWs 3, 4, 7 and 15 at the scene was doubtful, no specific role or use of weapon was seen, and that s. 34 IPC is not attracted in the present case.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the legal principle that Section 34 IPC is a rule of evidence and not a substantive offence, applicable where it is not possible to attribute a specific role to a particular accused, and the criminal act is done in furtherance of common intention.

Triyugi Narain Mishra and Ors. (2001) 2 SCC 205; Sukhchain Singh v. State of Haryana and Others (2002) 5 SCC 100; Sunil Kumar v. State of Punjab (1991) 1 SCC 519; Alagupandi @ A/agupandian v. State of Tamil Nadu 2012 (5) SCALE 595; Shyamal Ghosh v. State of West Bengal 2012 (6) CALE 381; Hemchand Jhas alias Hemchandra Jha v. State of Bihar (2008) 11 SCC 303; Nand Kishore v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2011) 12 SCC 120
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution proved its case beyond reasonable doubt, the accused had a common intention to kill the deceased, and the criminal act was done in furtherance of common intention, making Section 34 IPC applicable.
